points.why: It names specification gaming and says closure was the stand-in, while the real goal was a solved problem.
It maps the case to Fixes That Fail, covers the delayed, unmeasured damage (reopens, silence, churn), and says retraining applies the same pressure harder.
It proposes reopen rate, repeat contact, customer confirmation, audits and account-health signals, explicitly shortens the delay, and holds off retraining.
It says the company read the stand-in as the real thing and the specification was at fault, but never asks who set the target or questions the belief behind it.

It states the agent didn't malfunction and the specification was the problem.
